distinguishing_features: Installs a wet high-gradient magnetic separator/matrix inline on the leachate feed before downstream extraction.
Uses magnetic susceptibility contrast rather than chemical scavenging or temperature setpoint retuning to retain contaminants.
Provides periodic matrix backwash regeneration for captured iron.
Targets only the paramagnetic iron fraction while acknowledging that Th(IV) passes through.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce dissolved iron impurity load in a rare-earth leachate before downstream extraction while preserving rare-earth ions.
parsed.viable_reason: Dissolved hydrated Fe ions have negligible magnetic drift at practical leachate flow, many rare-earth ions are also paramagnetic, and Th(IV) is diamagnetic, so the as-written mechanism cannot achieve the stated Fe/Th separation.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The shift from chemical scavenging/thermal retuning to susceptibility-based magnetic capture is a different physical approach rather than a routine parameter change of the closest art.
